narrative: Markets are currently grappling with extreme volatility driven by the intersection of AI-sector governance concerns and looming geopolitical trade friction. While the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia initially sparked a massive rally, sentiment has rapidly soured due to bipartisan regulatory scrutiny and the threat of broad Section 301 tariffs on major trading partners. Economic resilience, evidenced by strong consumer confidence and retail earnings, is paradoxically complicating the Fed's path by keeping inflation expectations elevated. Investors are increasingly rotating into safe-haven assets as the sustainability of the AI-led rally faces its most significant test of the year. The market is now caught between the euphoria of AI infrastructure investment and the harsh reality of potential trade wars and restrictive monetary policy.

Nasdaq.why: The index is caught between massive gains from the Nvidia-led AI rally and mounting pressure from regulatory investigations and valuation concerns.

S&P 500.why: The index is struggling to maintain momentum as broad tariff fears and corporate earnings misses offset the optimism from resilient consumer spending.

Gold.why: Gold was not covered in the provided notes.

Oil.why: Brent crude has seen conflicting signals, with some analysts noting price easing to help inflation, while others observe a shift toward bullish sentiment.
